arxiv-2106-05371.title: Long-Range Order and Quantum Criticality in a Dissipative Spin Chain
arxiv-2106-05371.creator: Matthew W. Butcher, J. H. Pixley, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy
arxiv-2106-05371.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Matthew W. Butcher, J. H. Pixley, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy. Environmental interaction is a fundamental consideration in any controlled quantum system. While interaction with a dissipative bath can lead to decoherence, it can also provide desirable emergent effects including induced spin-spin correlations. In this paper we show that under quite general conditions, a dissipative bosonic bath can induce a long-range ordered phase, without the inclusion of any additional direct spin-spin couplings.

arxiv-2201-02639.description: Abstract As humans, we navigate a multimodal world, building a holistic understanding from all our senses. arxiv-2209-10852.creator: Keith Burghardt, Johannes H. Uhl, Kristina Lerman, Stefan Leyk
arxiv-2209-10852.description: Abstract The scaling relations between city attributes and population are emergent and ubiquitous aspects of urban growth. Quantifying these relations and understanding their theoretical foundation, however, is difficult due to the challenge of defining city boundaries and a lack of historical data to study city dynamics over time and space.

arxiv-2410-11051.title: Noise-enhanced Ballistic Expansion of Polariton Wave-packets in a Multimode Cavity
arxiv-2410-11051.creator: Ilia Tutunnikov, Md Qutubuddin, H. R. Sadeghpour, Jianshu Cao
arxiv-2410-11051.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ilia Tutunnikov, Md Qutubuddin, H. R. Sadeghpour, Jianshu Cao. Advances in optical measurements enable precise tracking of cavity polariton wave-packets across broad spatial and temporal ranges, but how dephasing reshapes their real-space dynamics over multiple time scales remains unclear. Here we show, using a stochastic multimode Tavis–Cummings model, that dephasing noise leads to a robust hierarchy of dynamical regimes comprising Rabi oscillation damping, center-of-mass slowdown, population relaxation, and ballistic-to-diffusive crossover, in the order of increasing time scales.

pmc-12656079.description: Reliable decoding of motor imagery (MI) from electroencephalographic signals remains a challenging problem due to their nonlinear, noisy, and non-stationary nature. pmc-13399498.title: Lamination of primary visual cortex in the macaque: Layer 5 subdivisions
pmc-13399498.creator: Bashir Ahmed, Alvaro Duque, Pasko Rakic, Zoltán Molnár
pmc-13399498.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Human and non‐human primates (NHPs) have a distinct lamination pattern of their primary visual cortex (V1) where layer 4 can be separated into four well‐defined sub‐laminae. Brodmann (1909) classified these into layers 4A, 4B, and 4C. Layer 4C can be further divided into 4Cα and 4Cβ based on inputs from the lateral geniculate magnocellular and parvocellular layers, respectively (Hubel & Wiesel, 1972; Lund, 1973).

pmc-13416722.title: A Single-IMU Wearable System with 1D U-Net for Knee Adduction Moment Waveform Reconstruction During Gait
pmc-13416722.creator: Hiroko Sakamoto, Hiroshi Yoshihara, Ayako Akiba, Kohei Nishizawa, Masaki Nagashima, Kengo Harato, Takeo Nagura, Masaya Nakamura
pmc-13416722.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A single tibial IMU with a 1D U-Net reconstructed knee adduction moment waveforms during gait.The waveform-derived peak KAM and KAM impulse showed positive associations with reference motion-analysis-derived values. What are the implications of the main findings? The system enables a clinically feasible assessment of medial knee loading without motion capture and force plates.

pmc-13636069.title: Autocrine signaling may regulate exercise-induced interleukin-6 release from human skeletal muscle
pmc-13636069.creator: Jonas Osted Hvidemose, Beckey Trinh, Alexandra Vassilieva, Anne-Sophie Worm Fenger, Peter Nissen Bjerring, Matthijs van Hall, Jens Otto Clemmesen, Sigurður þór Sigurðsson, Kirsten Møller, Gerrit van Hall, Mark A Febbraio, Bente K Pedersen, Peter Plomgaard, Helga Ellingsgaard
pmc-13636069.description: BackgroundContracting skeletal muscle releases interleukin-6 (IL-6) which is primarily cleared by the liver. The tissue-specific regulation of IL-6 and soluble IL-6 receptor (sIL-6R) kinetics remains, however, poorly understood. To characterize tissue-specific IL-6 and sIL-6R exchange during exercise, we combined simultaneous arteriovenous measurements across the contracting leg, splanchnic region, and the brain with, or without, pharmacological IL-6 receptor (IL-6R) blockade.

pmc-13650599.title: The molecular landscape of nodular fasciitis: novel USP6 fusions, genomic stability, and an exploratory clinicopathological model – a 20‐year retrospective study
pmc-13650599.creator: Kristijan Skok, Maximilian T Buchwald, Maria Anna Smolle, Theresa Godschachner, Andreas Leithner, Christian Viertler, Bernadette Liegl‐Atzwanger
pmc-13650599.description: Nodular fasciitis (NF) is a benign myofibroblastic neoplasm characterized by rapid growth and recurrent USP6 rearrangements. Despite its benign nature, NF may exhibit worrisome histologic or clinical features that mimic sarcoma, posing diagnostic challenges. The relationship between molecular diversity and morphologic heterogeneity remains incompletely understood.
